newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: TENNIS-AUSTRALIA COMPLETE IMPRESSIVE VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-AUSTRALIA COMPLETE IMPRESSIVE VICTORY.

text.p: Australia stayed on course for a return to the Fed Cup world group by completing an impressive 3-2 victory over South Africa in their group two tie at Westridge Park on Sunday.

Rachel McQuillan's second singles victory of the weekend, over South African number two Joannette Kruger, clinched the tie 3-1. South Africa took little consolation from victory for Mariaan de Swardt and Roslyn Fairbank-Nideffer in the dead doubles over Kristine Radford and Kerry-Ann Guse.
World number 13 Amanda Coetzer had kept alive South Africa's hopes of overturning Saturday's 2-0 deficit by beating Annabel Ellwood in three sets in the first reverse singles.

In blustery conditions Coetzer again looked out of touch as she lost the first set 6-1 to a player ranked 60 places below her. She finally rediscovered her form to drop only one game in the next two sets.
In the second reverse singles McQuillan saved one set point at 5-3 to set off on a run of seven successive winning games to take the first set against Kruger and race into a 3-0 lead in the second.
Kruger -- needing to win to keep South Africa in the tie -- clawed back to 4-4 but the Australian's cooler nerve paid off once again.

Australia now meet one of the world group one losers in a play-off for a place back in the top flight. South Africa must overcome a loser from the Europe/Africa zone to prevent a second successive relegation having been knocked out of the world group by Belgium last season.
